questions.question: What is an exception in Java?
options: A compilation error that prevents generating the bytecode
A runtime error that interrupts the normal flow of the program
A warning the compiler shows when it finds suspicious code
A special type of variable for handling errors
explanations: Compilation errors are not exceptions; they are detected before running the program.
Correct. An exception is an event that occurs at runtime and alters the normal flow of the program.
Compiler warnings are not exceptions; they are just notifications.
Exceptions are not variables; they are objects that represent errors.

questions.question: What is a checked exception?
options: An exception that is verified automatically at runtime
An exception verified by the compiler that must be handled or declared
An exception that only occurs with primitive data types
An exception thrown when a null value is checked
explanations: Checked exceptions are verified at compile time, not at runtime.
Correct. A checked exception is verified by the compiler, and the code must use try-catch or declare it with throws.
Checked exceptions have no relation to primitive types.
Checking null values does not define checked exceptions.

questions.question: What is an unchecked exception?
options: An exception the compiler does not force you to handle; it inherits from RuntimeException
An exception that must always be caught with try-catch
An exception that only occurs during compilation
An exception that requires using the throws keyword in every function
explanations: Correct. Unchecked exceptions (like NullPointerException) inherit from RuntimeException and do not require an explicit try-catch.
Unchecked exceptions do not force the use of try-catch; it is optional.
Exceptions occur at runtime, not during compilation.
Unchecked exceptions do not require the throws keyword in the method signature.

questions.question: What does the Error class represent in Java?
options: A minor error that can be ignored in the code
A serious system error that generally should not be attempted to be caught
An alternative way of writing checked exceptions
A type of custom exception created by the developer
explanations: Errors are not minor errors; they represent serious system failures.
Correct. Error represents serious JVM system problems like OutOfMemoryError or StackOverflowError, which normally should not be attempted to be handled.
Error is not an alternative to checked exceptions; it is a different category.
Error is a class from the Java API, not a custom exception.

questions.question: What is the main hierarchy of error handling in Java?
options: Error → Exception → RuntimeException
Exception → Error → Throwable
Throwable → Exception / Error
RuntimeException → Exception → Throwable
explanations: The order is inverted. Throwable is the parent class.
Exception is not a parent of Error. Both are children of Throwable.
Correct. Throwable is the root class and has two main children: Exception (exceptions) and Error (system errors).
RuntimeException is a child of Exception, not the other way around.
